reliability.rationale: Causal 300-minute calibration improves held-run MAE to 1.43487281 percentage points versus hold 5.47826699 and linear 7.79773109, but flexible control is better at 1.21103522. Two reserved runs only.

mechanism.rationale: Relaxation plus drift is compatible with induction but selectivity alone does not identify silver oxidation state, acid/metal pathways, or intermediates.

novelty.rationale: Existing source analyses and standard response families are disclosed. This review does not certify exhaustive literature novelty; the result is validated_extension.

significance.rationale: Potential short-horizon monitoring after a substantial per-run calibration budget, with gain over naive continuation but no best-model claim.

reproducibility.rationale: Equation, frozen coefficients, source audit, grouping, calibration and compact numerical evidence are inspectable. This scientific review does not replace the separately assigned computational replay.

impact.rationale: No operational intervention, cost/reliability improvement, or independent experimental deployment was measured. Potential utility is restricted to the stated task.

checks: Checked 120–300-minute slope/anchor calibration, 300–1500-minute score window, whole-run duplicate linkage, supplied selectivity rather than closure, and frozen-reference versus flexible/candidate results.
limitations: Only eight source runs, six development and two confirmation; condition changes are not independent reactor replications.
Per-run target prefix and slope are explicitly available; not cold-start catalyst prediction.
